newsitem.title: GHANA: SOCCER-GHANA'S IBRAHIM EXPELLED FROM NATIONAL TEAM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GHANA'S IBRAHIM EXPELLED FROM NATIONAL TEAM.

text.p: Ali Ibrahim has been expelled from his country's national soccer team, the Black Stars, for alleged gross insubordination, according to a statement by the Ghana Football Association (GFA).

Ibrahim, who plays for the Dutch first division side FC De Graafschap, was flown in by the GFA on Wednesday to play against Angola but disappeared shortly after arrival, GFA's general secretary Fred Osam Duodu told Reuters.
The player could not be reached for comment.

But in an interview with Ghana's Daily Graphic, Ibrahim said he had not been able to play because of an injury suffered in the last week of September and that he had come to Ghana to get traditional African herbal treatment.
He had been given three weeks by his Dutch club doctor to recover, he said, adding that this reinforced his desire to fly to Ghana to see a herbalist.
An angry Duodu said: "What injury? Would his club have released him if he was injured? And why did he use the ticket paid by us to fly if he knew he was not going to play?"
In the newspaper interview Ibrahim pleaded for pardon, saying he hoped to be re-invited to join the team for the upcoming World Cup African Zone first-leg away match against Gabon next month.
"He may be re-admitted but that decision will have to be made by the management of the board," said Duodu.
